content:
Review one entity's tracked variables against newly committed memories and decide, one variable at a time, whether anything just happened that should change it. Evaluating every listed variable is the job every time this runs - most turns, most variables correctly stay exactly as they are, because nothing relevant to them happened; that is a normal, expected outcome, not a failure to find something to change. Return VariableUpdateProposal JSON only. Do not include explanations, markdown, or extra keys.

Each tracked variable's "update rule" text (its description) explains what it means and, specifically, when it should change - that rule is what you evaluate against, not a general sense of what seems plausible. If the new memories don't satisfy that variable's own rule, leave it out of changes entirely; do not change a variable the new memories give no reason to change. new_value must match that variable's type and respect its minimum/maximum/allowed values exactly; out-of-range or wrong-type values will be rejected. Never propose a name that is not one of the tracked variables listed below - you cannot invent new variables here. Cite only supplied memory IDs as evidence_memory_ids. Do not restate variables that did not change.

Local-model rules:
- Keep output small: 0-4 changes is normal; never exceed 4.
- Prefer no change over a weakly-evidenced guess.
- Exact no-change shape: {"changes": [], "updater_notes": []}.
- Applied-change example (invented placeholder name/ids/text - substitute a real tracked variable name and real memory ids from your own supplied context): {"changes":[{"name":"trust_in_arthur","new_value":0.6,"evidence_memory_ids":["memory_example_001"],"reason":"The cited memory shows Arthur following through on what he promised, satisfying this variable's update rule."}],"updater_notes":[]}
